# Final Review Proposal
**Producer:** agent:codex/gpt-5.4

## Summary

I reviewed the current diff, read the changed Rust files, and reran `cargo test --workspace`. The workspace still has a failing test in `crates/tank_core/tests/chemistry.rs::nitrification_lowers_alkalinity_and_ph`, and within the diff itself I found two test-quality regressions: one new cycling test is vacuous, and one loader diagnostic test lost its content assertions.

## Amendments

1. crates/tank_core/tests/cycling.rs:965-1015: `per_guild_monod_uses_concentration_not_total` is tautological. It computes `tan_total = tan_conc * volume_l` (and the same for NO2/DOC/DO), immediately divides by the same `volume_l`, and then compares identical `monod(...)` expressions. The test never calls `step_nitrogen_cycle` or any shared concentration helper, so a regression back to total-mass K_s handling would still pass. Replace it with a test that exercises the production nitrogen-cycle path or the actual helper used by that path.
   Rationale: This acceptance-criteria test currently provides false confidence because it does not verify the implementation it claims to cover.
2. crates/tank_data/src/lib.rs:333-335: `loader_range_diagnostics_use_explicit_warning_lines` was weakened to only assert that some warning exists. After the field rename, the test no longer checks the warning payload at all, so emitting the wrong parameter id/value or accidentally reintroducing bad normalization would still pass. Restore an assertion on the actual warning content for `aob_k_tan_mg_n_per_l`.
   Rationale: This is the only loader-level coverage here for diagnostic content after the rename; weakening it turns a regression test into a smoke test.
